blocks.text: MAE SOT, Thailand — She starts work at 4 p.m., using her company-issued iPhone 14. Assigned to Line 1, she randomly dials phone numbers belonging to people more than 8,000 miles away. Denise (not her real name) sighs when someone answers. On the other end is an elderly American man, probably sitting on a couch watching a television that has been on for hours. The moment he answers, he becomes a potential victim. The call is immediately transferred to Line 2, then to Line 3. Meanwhile, Denise just wants to rest. She has been working 12-hour shifts since arriving in July […]... Keep on reading: Filipinos on the line: Inside a Myanmar scam operation
